newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African police fire teargas at Joburg protesters.
newsitem.headline: S.African police fire teargas at Joburg protesters.

text.p: South African police on Thursday used stun grenades and teargas to disperse protesting residents of coloured (mixed-race) areas of Johannesburg, a spokesman said.
Police said hundreds of protesters blocked major roads as coloured residents of Johannesburg and surrounding suburbs embarked on a stayaway called by a civic body.
"We used stun grenades and teargas to disperse people," police spokesman Mark Reynolds told Reuters.
The stayaway was called by the South Western Joint Civics Association (Sowjeca) to protest threats by municipalities to cut services because of non-payment.
Reynolds said protesters blocked roads in coloured suburbs west of Johannesburg with burning tyres and garbage bins.
State radio reported that provincial safety and security minister Jessie Duarte warned that any acts of intimidation to enforce Thursday's stayaway would be met with strong police action.
Reynolds said police were hesitant to arrest protesters to avoid inciting the crowds.
"We don't want to incite them. They have been warned and we are managing the situation on an ongoing basis," he added.
